assessments.reason: Group investment is large and company-reported deployment is real evidence of scale. But nine-month 2026 asset cash purchases declined YoY, and the reviewed sources do not isolate BYD-owned charging capex.
missing_evidence: Charging-specific cash investment and ownership contracts

assessments.reason: Reported use and broader compatibility support customer interest; incremental vehicle sales, willingness to pay and mature utilization are not identified.

An open partner-built ecosystem can grow rapidly but does not establish exclusive control or retained economic rents. Competing fast-charging routes exist; comparative field performance remains unverified.
Cash investment burden and quarterly recovery can coexist. No causal attribution to charging or valuation comparison is available. 2027-2030 outcomes have not resolved.

conflicts.description: Q3 profit recovered while nine-month profit declined
conflicts.explanation: Different observation windows; both can be correct. A consensus forecast miss is not established by YoY changes.

conflicts.description: Charging rollout grew while year-to-date group asset cash purchases declined
conflicts.explanation: Group spending versus network count and annual versus partial-year comparisons differ. Partner construction and investment timing are plausible contributors, but their quantitative contribution is unknown.

conflicts.description: Open access may increase traffic but reduce exclusivity
conflicts.explanation: Traffic effects and profit capture are different targets. Openness does not rule out economic rents, but neither scale nor third-party usage proves them.

next_actions: Collect operating station-days and monthly delivered kWh by station vintage; exclude promotions when measuring paid retention.
Obtain representative operator agreements to separate capex funding, asset ownership, net service-fee share and replacement obligations.
Compare matched city/model cohorts before and after effective coverage, while checking rollout selection, parallel trends, subsidies and competitor launches.
Track 2027-2030 incremental capital returns and vehicle contribution after charging subsidies; avoid double-counting benefits.
